First, we apply the addition principle, adding $8$ to both sides: \begin{align} -2x -8 &\le 4 \\[5pt] -2x -8+8 &\le 4 +8 \\[5pt] -2x + 0 &\le 12 \\[5pt] -2x &\le 12 \end{align}

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-2.$

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

\begin{align} \require{cancel} -2x \,\,&{\color{blue}\le\,\,} 12 \\[5pt] \dfrac{-2x}{-2} \,&{\color{red}\ge\,\,} \dfrac{12}{-2} \\[5pt] \dfrac{\cancel{-2}x}{\cancel{-2}} \,&{\color{red}\ge\,\,} {-6} \\[5pt] x \,\,&{\color{red}\ge\,} {-6} \end{align}

Therefore, the solution is $x\ge -6.$

question.text: The solution to the inequality $-10x - 13 < 17$ is
question.explanation:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $13$ to both sides: \begin{align} -10x - 13 &< 17 \\[5pt] -10x - 13 + 13 &< 17 + 13 \\[5pt] -10x + 0 &< 30 \\[5pt] -10x &< 30 \end{align}

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-10.$

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

\begin{align} \require{cancel} -10x \,\,&{\color{blue}<\,\,} 30\\[5pt] \dfrac{-10x}{-10} \,&{\color{red}>\,\,} \dfrac{30}{-10} \\[5pt] \dfrac{\cancel{-10}x}{\cancel{-10}} \,&{\color{red}>\,\,} {-3} \\[5pt] x \,\,&{\color{red}>\,} {-3} \end{align}

Therefore, the solution is $x \bbox[4pt,Gainsboro]{\color{red} > } \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ -3 }.$

question.text: The solution to the inequality $2 \lt 9y - 7$ is $y$
question.explanation:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $7$ to both sides: \begin{align*} 2 &\lt 9y-7 \\[3pt] 2+7 &\lt 9y-7+7\\[3pt] 9 &\lt 9y + 0 \\[3pt] 9 &\lt 9y \end{align*}

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $9{:}$ \begin{align*} \require{cancel} 9 &\lt 9y \\[5pt] \dfrac{9}{9} &\lt \dfrac{9y}{9} \\[5pt] 1 &\lt \dfrac{\cancel{9}y}{\cancel{9}} \\[5pt] 1 &\lt y \end{align*}

Finally, let's swap the left and right-hand sides so that the variable is on the left-hand side. Remember, we also need to flip the inequality. \[ y \gt 1 \]

Therefore, the solution is $y\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \gt }\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 1}.$
